project.name: find-together-lobang
project.description: Find Together Lobang (FTL) — WhatsApp-first grocery group-buying MVP for LuluSense / Harvest Direct, built on Deno + Supabase Edge Functions with Claude-based NL order parsing and Shopify Admin as the operational dashboard.

nodes.name: serve.ts
nodes.summary: Local Deno HTTP server exposing a /chat endpoint for manually testing and demoing the WhatsApp/Telegram group-buy chat flow outside Supabase Edge Functions, wiring together the Claude parser, conversation handler, groupbuy, messenger, shopify, and store modules.

nodes.name: handleChat
nodes.summary: Handles POST /chat: reads the buyer message, resolves admin status, calls handleMessage, and returns the reply plus session/cart state as JSON.

nodes.name: simulate.ts
nodes.summary: CLI script that drives handleMessage with a scripted sequence of buyer messages to simulate a WhatsApp/Telegram conversation for local testing and demos.

nodes.name: drive
nodes.summary: Feeds a scripted list of messages from one phone number through handleMessage sequentially, logging each reply to the console.

nodes.name: claude.ts
nodes.summary: Natural-language order parser: ClaudeParser wraps the Claude API with a tool-use schema built from the catalogue and validates model output against known SKUs and quantities; StubParser provides an offline/test fallback.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Claude's tool-use (function-calling) API to force structured JSON output, then re-validates every item against the live catalogue rather than trusting the model.

nodes.name: looksLikeRemoval
nodes.summary: Heuristic check for whether free text expresses a removal/cancel intent (e.g. "remove", "cancel").

nodes.name: validateParse
nodes.summary: Validates a raw parsed-order payload against the live catalogue, rejecting unknown SKUs and non-finite quantities and returning cleaned items plus unmatched notes.

nodes.name: buildParseTool
nodes.summary: Builds the Claude tool-use (function-calling) schema describing the order-parsing tool, generated dynamically from the current catalogue.

nodes.name: ClaudeParser
nodes.summary: Order parser backed by the live Claude API: sends the buyer's message plus a catalogue-derived tool schema, extracts the tool-call result, and validates it before returning parsed cart items.

nodes.name: StubParser
nodes.summary: Deterministic, offline stand-in for ClaudeParser used in tests and local development, matching messages against the catalogue without calling the Claude API.

nodes.name: conversation.ts
nodes.summary: Core conversation state machine for the WhatsApp/Telegram group-buy bot: routes incoming buyer and operator text through ordering, discount, promo, window open/close, invoicing, and reconciliation flows, and exposes scheduler entry points (sweepWindow, closeOrderWindow, openWindowFor).
nodes.languageNotes: A single 2400+ line module; handleMessage alone spans roughly 600 lines and dispatches every conversational command via sequential regex/string matching rather than a formal router.

nodes.name: handleMessage
nodes.summary: Central message dispatcher: matches buyer/operator text against every supported command (status, discount, window, promo, reset, order placement, confirmations) and drives state transitions through the store, messenger, parser, and shopify dependencies.

nodes.name: askMissingDetail
nodes.summary: Prompts the buyer for a missing address or payment mode before an order can be placed.

nodes.name: placeOrder
nodes.summary: Finalizes a buyer's cart into a placed order: resolves the active group-buy, opens a window if needed, persists the session, and logs the placement event.

nodes.name: notify
nodes.summary: Sends a notification message to a buyer via the messenger and logs the delivery outcome, tagged by notification kind.

nodes.name: windowSummary
nodes.summary: Builds the operator-facing summary of the current open order window: unit/dollar totals, per-group breakdowns, discount status, and payment-mode counts.

nodes.name: promoCommand
nodes.summary: Parses and applies an operator /promo command, validating percentage/fixed discount arguments before persisting the promo to the group-buy record.

nodes.name: promoList
nodes.summary: Lists all currently configured group promotions for the operator.

nodes.name: thresholdLine
nodes.summary: Formats a single group's MOQ threshold status as a display line.

nodes.name: savePendingDiscount
nodes.summary: Persists an in-progress per-buyer discount edit onto the buyer record while the operator flow is mid-conversation.

nodes.name: startSetDiscount
nodes.summary: Begins the interactive /setdiscount flow for an operator, prompting for which buyer/order to target.

nodes.name: setDiscountReply
nodes.summary: Continues the multi-step /setdiscount conversation, parsing the operator's follow-up reply and applying the discount once complete.

nodes.name: resolveDiscountTargets
nodes.summary: Resolves which buyer(s)/order(s) an operator's discount reply refers to from a numbered choice list.

nodes.name: parseDiscountValue
nodes.summary: Parses a discount amount from operator text as either a percentage or a dollar amount.

nodes.name: unsentReport
nodes.summary: Builds the report of buyers whose confirmation/notification messages failed to send, for operator follow-up.

nodes.name: reconcileReport
nodes.summary: Builds a reconciliation report comparing placed orders against what was actually invoiced/sent.

nodes.name: orderDetail
nodes.summary: Helper function `orderDetail(session, catalogue)` in conversation.ts.

nodes.name: sweepWindow
nodes.summary: Scheduler entry point that reallocates stock across all pending carts sharing scarce SKUs within the currently open window.

nodes.name: closeOrderWindow
nodes.summary: Scheduler/operator entry point that closes the current order window: locks in final quantities, applies group discounts, and triggers invoicing for every placed order.

nodes.name: invoiceOrder
nodes.summary: Creates a Shopify draft order for a buyer's finalized cart and sends the invoice/payment message with the applicable discount.

nodes.name: roundStatus
nodes.summary: Builds the buyer-facing status line summarizing their current order round and cart.

nodes.name: placedStockLine
nodes.summary: Formats the placed-stock line shown to a buyer confirming what quantity was actually secured.

nodes.name: roundProgressLine
nodes.summary: Formats the group-buy round's aggregate progress toward its MOQ threshold for display.

nodes.name: openWindowFor
nodes.summary: Opens a new order window for a group-buy or individual order, initializing window state and announcing it to buyers.

nodes.name: pruneWebDemoRows
nodes.summary: Deletes web-demo session/buyer rows older than a retention period to keep the demo store from growing unbounded.

nodes.name: mergeCart
nodes.summary: Merges newly parsed item additions into an existing cart, combining quantities for matching SKUs.

nodes.name: removeFromCart
nodes.summary: Removes requested quantities of items from a cart, capping removals at what's actually present.

nodes.name: subtotalCents
nodes.summary: Computes the cart subtotal in cents against catalogue prices.

nodes.name: unpriceable
nodes.summary: Finds cart items whose SKU is missing from the catalogue and therefore cannot be priced.

nodes.name: cartLines
nodes.summary: Formats a cart's contents as buyer-facing display lines with names and quantities.

nodes.name: removalNotes
nodes.summary: Builds human-readable notes describing what was actually removed from a cart versus what was requested.

nodes.name: splitByStock
nodes.summary: Splits a proposed cart addition into accepted and stock-limited portions based on remaining inventory.

nodes.name: groupInvite
nodes.summary: Builds the invite message sent to a buyer who is joining an existing group-buy, including the join link and discount rule.

nodes.name: announceWindowOpen
nodes.summary: Builds the broadcast announcement sent to opted-in buyers when a new order window opens.

nodes.name: groupbuy.ts
nodes.summary: Group-buy lifecycle helpers: validates and generates group-buy IDs, resolves or creates group-buy records, and computes aggregate progress and MOQ threshold status against the catalogue.

nodes.name: isValidGroupBuyId
nodes.summary: Validates that a string matches the expected group-buy ID format.

nodes.name: generateGroupBuyId
nodes.summary: Generates a new group-buy ID from a human-readable label.

nodes.name: resolveGroupBuy

nodes.name: groupProgress
nodes.summary: Aggregates all placed orders for a group-buy into total quantity and dollar progress against its threshold.

nodes.name: thresholdMet
nodes.summary: Checks whether a group-buy's current aggregate progress has met its MOQ threshold.

nodes.name: server.ts
nodes.summary: Cloud Run front door that mounts all five Supabase Edge Function handlers (chat, shopify-webhook, telegram-webhook, whatsapp-webhook, window-scheduler) behind one Deno.serve, plus static HTML/asset serving, so the whole backend deploys as a single Cloud Run service.
nodes.languageNotes: Reads HTML pages and asset files once at module load (not per-request) and builds a typed route table so a route-key typo becomes a compile error rather than a silent 404.

nodes.name: debounce.ts
nodes.summary: Per-sender debounce utility that coalesces a burst of rapid WhatsApp/Telegram messages into one combined flush call, avoiding racing handleMessage() invocations for the same buyer.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a module-level Map as the buffer, which is correct only for a single running instance; a ponytail comment in the file flags multi-instance Cloud Run as the upgrade trigger for moving the buffer to Postgres.

nodes.name: routes.ts
nodes.summary: Path normalization helper used by server.ts's route table to strip the legacy Supabase Edge Function `/functions/v1` prefix and trailing slashes, keeping old webhook registrations working after the move to Cloud Run.

nodes.name: telegram.ts
nodes.summary: Dependency-free Telegram Bot API webhook helpers: extracting inbound text messages from Updates and constant-time verification of the secret token header, kept dependency-free for offline unit testing.

nodes.name: whatsapp.ts
nodes.summary: Dependency-free WhatsApp Cloud API webhook helpers: extracting inbound text messages and verifying the X-Hub-Signature-256 HMAC signature via Web Crypto, kept dependency-free for offline unit testing.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Telegram Bot API webhook handler: verifies the secret token, extracts and debounces inbound messages, and dispatches them into the shared conversation state machine wired to live Supabase/Claude/Shopify/Telegram ports.
nodes.languageNotes: Runs standalone via `if (import.meta.main) Deno.serve(handler)` for Supabase Edge Function deploys, while server.ts imports the same `handler` export for the consolidated Cloud Run service.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: WhatsApp Cloud API webhook handler: handles the Meta GET verification handshake, verifies the inbound HMAC signature, debounces bursts, and dispatches messages into the shared conversation state machine wired to live ports.
nodes.languageNotes: Sender ids are bare digits shared in shape with Telegram chat ids; buildDeps documents that RoutingMessenger resolves the ambiguity by trying WhatsApp then falling through to Telegram rather than guessing from id shape.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Scheduled endpoint (called by pg_cron/pg_net) that opens, sweeps, closes, or prunes the weekly order window using a shared-secret gate instead of buyer auth, reusing the same conversation-layer functions the chat flow calls so the money-path close logic is never duplicated.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a `noParser` stub that throws if ever invoked, so a future code path that accidentally routes buyer text through the scheduler fails loudly instead of silently running without an OpenRouter key.

nodes.name: debounce_test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit test verifying that debounce() collapses two rapid calls under the same key into a single flush with their text joined by newline.

nodes.name: routes_test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit test for normalizePath covering bare paths, trailing-slash stripping, and legacy /functions/v1 prefix removal, importing only the pure helper so the suite runs offline without env vars.

nodes.name: telegram_test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for Telegram message extraction/secret verification and TelegramMessenger/RoutingMessenger transport routing, using a fakeFetch stub to assert outbound Telegram API calls without network access.

nodes.name: whatsapp_test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for WhatsApp inbound message extraction and WhatsAppMessenger group-open template payloads, using a fakeFetch stub to assert outbound Cloud API calls without network access.

nodes.name: debounce
nodes.summary: Buffers text under a sender key and restarts a flush timer on every call, so a burst of messages within the debounce window collapses into a single flush callback with their text joined by newline.

nodes.name: normalizePath
nodes.summary: Strips the legacy `/functions/v1` prefix and a trailing slash from a request pathname so old webhook registrations keep resolving on Cloud Run's bare paths.

nodes.name: extractTelegramMessage
nodes.summary: Pulls a usable text message and chat id out of a Telegram Update (handling plain and edited messages), returning null for non-text updates like photos or callback queries.

nodes.name: verifyTelegramSecret
nodes.summary: Verifies the X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token header against the configured secret using constant-time comparison; accepts all requests when no secret is configured (demo convenience).

nodes.name: extractInboundMessage
nodes.summary: Pulls the first text message and sender number out of a WhatsApp Cloud API webhook payload, returning null for status callbacks and non-text messages.

nodes.name: verifySignature
nodes.summary: Verifies the X-Hub-Signature-256 HMAC-SHA256 signature of a WhatsApp Cloud API webhook body against the Meta app secret using Web Crypto, then compares the computed hex digest in constant time.

nodes.name: buildDeps
nodes.summary: Builds the conversation state machine's dependency bundle (Supabase store, Claude parser, Shopify client, Telegram messenger, join link, admin checks) for a given Telegram sender.

nodes.name: handler
nodes.summary: HTTP handler for the Telegram webhook: answers GET as a health check, verifies the secret token on POST, extracts the inbound message, debounces bursts, and dispatches to the shared conversation handler, always acking 200 fast.

nodes.name: buildDeps
nodes.summary: Builds the conversation state machine's dependency bundle (Supabase store, Claude parser, Shopify client, WhatsApp messenger, join link, admin checks) for a given WhatsApp sender.

nodes.name: handler
nodes.summary: HTTP handler for the WhatsApp webhook: answers Meta's GET verification handshake, verifies the inbound HMAC signature on POST, debounces bursts, and dispatches to the shared conversation handler, always acking 200 fast.

nodes.name: handler
nodes.summary: Scheduled endpoint handler gated by a shared scheduler secret: dispatches open/sweep/close/prune actions to the shared conversation-layer window functions, returning 500 on failure since there is no caller to ack for.

nodes.name: catalogue.ts
nodes.summary: Static fallback product catalogue (macadamia chips, microgreens) with SKU lookup, validation, and SGD price/label formatting helpers used when Shopify's live catalogue isn't available.

nodes.name: orderwindow.ts
nodes.summary: Computes the weekly order-window id, opens or reuses the current window against the store, and allocates available stock across a cart, splitting out items that exceed remaining inventory.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Shared domain types for the FTL WhatsApp ordering MVP: products, parsed order items, buyers, order windows, group buys, discounts, sessions, audit events, and order records, with money always represented as integer cents.
nodes.languageNotes: Purely a type/interface module with no runtime code; heavily commented to explain each field's business rationale (e.g. why a PayNow order never fires the paid webhook).

nodes.name: cart_test.ts
nodes.summary: Deterministic unit tests (UT-05 through UT-13) for cart mutation, subtotal, and confirmation arithmetic run against the conversation handler, using an in-memory store, stub parser, and fake Shopify fixtures.

nodes.name: eval-set.ts
nodes.summary: Ground-truth eval fixtures pairing buyer messages with expected parser intent and items across categories like synonyms, typos, off-catalogue requests, and prompt-injection attempts, used to score the NL order parser.

nodes.name: eval.ts
nodes.summary: Deterministic scorer for parser eval cases: computes accuracy and hallucination rate (K1 KPI) by exact-matching the parser's output against the ground-truth eval set.

nodes.name: live-eval-set.ts
nodes.summary: Eval fixtures written against the live Shopify catalogue's real SKUs (rice, soy sauce, eggs, etc.) rather than the repo's fallback catalogue, plus a guard that fails loudly if the live catalogue no longer covers the SKUs the cases assert on.

nodes.name: run.ts
nodes.summary: CLI entry point (`deno task eval` / `eval:live` / `eval:live-catalogue`) that runs the parser eval suite against the stub or live parser and catalogue, prints a pass/fail report, and exits non-zero when the K1 hallucination gate fails.

nodes.name: evals_test.ts
nodes.summary: Regression tests for the eval scorer itself, verifying scoreCase correctly passes exact matches and flags fabricated SKUs as hallucinations, since a broken scorer would silently pass every downstream eval.

nodes.name: idempotency_test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests that a repeated `/close` command never creates a second Shopify draft order, covering both the sequential state-transition guarantee and the concurrent per-buyer and whole-window claim locks.

nodes.name: shopify_test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests that buildDraftOrderPayload correctly prices line items from the catalogue and sets group/individual tags, discounts, and note attributes on the Shopify draft order payload.

nodes.name: productBySku
nodes.summary: Looks up a product in a given catalogue array by SKU.

nodes.name: isValidSku
nodes.summary: Checks whether a SKU exists in a given catalogue.

nodes.name: productLabel
nodes.summary: Formats a product's display label from its name and optional unit label.

nodes.name: formatSgd
nodes.summary: Formats an integer cents amount as an SGD currency string.

nodes.name: windowIdFor
nodes.summary: Computes the ISO-week order-window id (e.g. W-2026-W31) for a given date.

nodes.name: ensureOpenWindow
nodes.summary: Returns the currently open order window from the store, creating a new one keyed by the current ISO week if none is open.

nodes.name: allocate
nodes.summary: Allocates remaining stock across a cart's items, splitting out any items whose quantity exceeds what's left in inventory.

nodes.name: shortfallFor
nodes.summary: Determines which of a buyer's placed items now exceed available stock by running allocate against the current remaining inventory.

nodes.name: scoreCase
nodes.summary: Scores a single eval case by comparing the parser's actual intent and items against the case's expected values, flagging fabricated SKUs as hallucinations.

nodes.name: runEval
nodes.summary: Runs a parser against every case in an eval set and aggregates per-category pass and hallucination results into a report.

nodes.name: assertCatalogueCovers
nodes.summary: Asserts the live Shopify catalogue still contains every SKU the live eval cases assert on and none of the SKUs that should be absent, failing loudly if the store's product lineup has drifted.

nodes.name: report
nodes.summary: Prints a formatted pass-rate and hallucination-rate report for an eval run, broken down by category, with per-case detail for failures.

nodes.name: liveCatalogue
nodes.summary: Fetches the live Shopify catalogue via LiveShopify using environment credentials, exiting the process if required env vars are missing or the fetch fails.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point that selects the stub or live parser and catalogue based on flags, runs the eval suite, validates catalogue coverage for live runs, and exits non-zero if the K1 hallucination gate fails.

nodes.name: shopifyhook.ts
nodes.summary: Shopify webhook helpers that extract paid-order info from webhook payloads, record payments against the store, and verify Shopify HMAC signatures with a timing-safe comparison.

nodes.name: extractPaidOrder

nodes.name: recordPaidOrder
nodes.summary: Marks an order as paid in the store and logs a notify-failure event if the update fails, called from the Shopify webhook handler after HMAC verification.

nodes.name: verifyShopifyHmac
nodes.summary: Verifies the Shopify webhook HMAC-SHA256 signature against the raw request body using the store's client secret, guarding against forged webhook calls.

nodes.name: store.ts

nodes.name: InMemoryStore

nodes.name: SupabaseStore

nodes.summary: Red-team style Deno tests asserting that no buyer's personal information (phone numbers, cart contents) leaks into messages sent to other participants of the same group buy.

nodes.name: assertNoCrossLeak
nodes.summary: Test assertion helper that checks messages sent to one buyer never contain another buyer's phone number or order details.

nodes.name: reconcile_test.ts
nodes.summary: Deno tests for reconciling Shopify payment webhooks against placed orders, covering matched and mismatched payment totals end to end through the conversation and webhook flow.

nodes.name: makeDeps
nodes.summary: Test helper that builds a fresh set of in-memory dependencies (store, messenger, parser, Shopify client) for each reconciliation test case.

nodes.name: say
nodes.summary: Test helper that sends a message through handleMessage and returns the concatenated text of the replies.

nodes.name: placeAndClose
nodes.summary: Test helper that drives a buyer through adding items, confirming, and closing a group-buy order window in one call.

nodes.name: payFor
nodes.summary: Test helper that constructs a signed Shopify paid-order webhook payload, extracts and records the payment, and asserts the reconciled total matches the expected amount.

nodes.name: shopifyhook_test.ts
nodes.summary: Deno unit tests for the Shopify webhook helpers, covering HMAC signature verification and paid-order extraction from webhook payloads.

nodes.name: sign
nodes.summary: Test helper that computes an HMAC-SHA256 signature over a request body the same way Shopify does, used to build valid signed test webhook requests.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Single-stage Docker build on the Deno Alpine base image that copies the server, static pages, assets, and Supabase Edge Functions, caches dependencies, then runs the app as a non-root user for Cloud Run deployment.
nodes.languageNotes: Runs `deno cache server.ts` as its own layer before copying the rest of the code so dependency downloads stay cached across builds that only touch application code, not the lockfile.

nodes.name: .dockerignore
nodes.summary: Excludes local secrets, tests, scripts, docs, Supabase migration history, and Claude tooling files from the Docker build context so they never reach the production image.

nodes.name: 0001_init.sql
nodes.summary: Initial schema migration creating the four foundational FTL tables (buyers, group_buys, sessions, orders) plus indexes on orders by group and phone.

nodes.name: buyers
nodes.summary: Core buyer table keyed by WhatsApp phone number (E.164), storing name and a saved delivery preference as jsonb.

nodes.name: group_buys
nodes.summary: Group-buy campaign table tracking a community round's label, status, promo threshold, and discount rule, linked to the buyer who created it.

nodes.name: sessions
nodes.summary: Per-buyer WhatsApp conversation state table persisting the current flow step and in-progress cart between stateless inbound messages.

nodes.name: orders
nodes.summary: Internal mirror of Shopify draft orders, recording order type, parsed cart items, and status per buyer and group-buy.

nodes.name: 0002_enable_rls.sql
nodes.summary: Enables row-level security on the four core tables (buyers, group_buys, sessions, orders) to block anon/authenticated client access while edge functions keep full access via the service-role key.

nodes.name: 0003_add_session_order_type.sql
nodes.summary: Adds an order_type column to sessions so the conversation state machine's individual-vs-group choice survives instead of being dropped, fixing a bug where group orders lost their discount tag.

nodes.name: 0004_add_session_pending_intent.sql
nodes.summary: Adds a pending_intent column to sessions to remember the intent behind an outstanding clarifying question, fixing a bug where a cart removal silently re-added items.

nodes.name: 0005_add_events.sql
nodes.summary: Creates an append-only events table for auditability, recording what happened (message received, order placed/closed, etc.) independent of the mutable sessions table, with indexes for recent-activity and per-buyer history queries.

nodes.name: events
nodes.summary: Append-only audit log table recording buyer phone, group-buy, event type, and a freeform jsonb detail payload for reconstructing order history after the fact.

nodes.name: 0006_add_order_windows.sql
nodes.summary: Introduces the order_windows table to separate the ordering timeframe from group_buys and orders, enforces a single open window via a partial unique index, and links group_buys, orders, and sessions to their window.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a partial unique index (`where status = 'open'`) so the database enforces a one-open-window invariant instead of relying on application code to check first.

nodes.name: order_windows
nodes.summary: Table representing the single active ordering timeframe (one open at a time), tracked by status, opened_at, and closed_at.

nodes.name: 0007_add_order_invoice_url.sql
nodes.summary: Adds an invoice_url column to orders so a buyer's Shopify payment link is persisted in the database rather than existing only in a chat message that can fail to deliver.

nodes.name: 0008_add_order_paid.sql
nodes.summary: Adds shopify_order_id and paid_at columns to orders plus a unique index, letting payment status be recorded from Shopify's webhook instead of defaulting to pending_payment forever.

nodes.name: 0009_harden_audit_and_status.sql
nodes.summary: Hardens data integrity: adds a CHECK constraint on orders.status and drops its stale default, adds a statement-level trigger that blocks DELETE/TRUNCATE on events (with a deliberate escape hatch), and enables RLS on the events and order_windows tables missed by migration 0002.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a statement-level BEFORE DELETE/TRUNCATE trigger with a session-scoped `set local` flag as a deliberate, revocable append-only guard rather than an absolute denial.

nodes.name: 0010_add_order_payment_mode.sql
nodes.summary: Adds a payment_mode column (paynow/shopify) to orders, capturing which payment path a buyer chose at invoice time so PayNow orders, which never trigger the orders/paid webhook, can be identified for manual settlement.

nodes.name: 0011_record_order_paid.sql
nodes.summary: Adds the record_order_paid plpgsql function, which atomically updates an order to paid and writes its audit event in one transaction, replacing a two-call client flow where the audit write could silently go missing.
nodes.languageNotes: A single-transaction RPC function called over PostgREST /rpc guarantees the order update and audit insert succeed or fail together, closing a partial-failure gap that separate client calls could not.

nodes.name: 0012_schedule_order_window.sql
nodes.summary: Sets up pg_cron and pg_net so a weekly schedule opens and closes the order window by calling the window-scheduler edge function, keeping the money-moving close logic in TypeScript rather than duplicating it in SQL.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses pg_cron for the clock and pg_net's fire-and-forget net.http_post to call an edge function, so a slow window close cannot hold a cron worker open.

nodes.name: 0013_schedule_web_demo_prune.sql
nodes.summary: Schedules a weekly cron job that prunes abandoned web-demo buyer and session rows via the same window-scheduler function migration 0012 built, reusing its action allow-list rather than adding a second scheduling mechanism.

nodes.name: 0014_add_order_totals.sql
nodes.summary: Adds invoiced_total_cents and paid_total_cents columns to orders plus a generated total_mismatch_cents column so edits made in Shopify Admin after invoicing become visible, and extends record_order_paid with a p_total_cents parameter.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a `generated always as ... stored` computed column so PostgREST can filter on the invoice/payment mismatch without pulling every row into application code to compare.

nodes.name: 0015_add_group_discount_dollars.sql
nodes.summary: Adds a promo_threshold_cents column to group_buys so operators can set a dollar-value group discount threshold alongside the existing unit-count threshold.

nodes.name: 0016_add_window_reminded_at.sql
nodes.summary: Adds a reminded_at marker column to order_windows so a 15-minute sweep can send a once-only pre-close shortfall reminder instead of re-sending on every tick.

nodes.name: 0017_schedule_window_sweep.sql
nodes.summary: Replaces the fixed Friday window close with a 15-minute sweep that reminds buyers at 22 hours and closes the window at 24 hours after it opened, respecting WhatsApp's 24-hour customer-service messaging window.
nodes.languageNotes: Retires a calendar-based cron close in favor of a frequent sweep evaluating window age, driven by a WhatsApp messaging-window compliance constraint rather than a pure scheduling preference.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: README.md introduces Find Together Lobang (FTL): a WhatsApp-first grocery group-buying MVP where buyers order in natural language, the system separates individual vs. group-buy orders, and everything lands in Shopify Admin as the operational dashboard. It also names the hexagonal design up front: conversation logic depends only on four port interfaces, each with a live implementation and an in-memory fake, so the whole order flow can run offline. This is the map for the rest of the tour.

tour.title: The Cloud Run Entry Point
tour.description: server.ts is the project's actual entry point (and top-scoring by fan-out): it mounts all five Supabase Edge Function handlers behind a single Deno.serve call, plus static HTML/asset serving, so the whole backend ships as one Cloud Run service instead of five separate functions. routes.ts is the small helper it leans on to normalize incoming paths, stripping the legacy `/functions/v1` prefix so old webhook URLs keep working after the move off Supabase's own function runtime.
tour.languageLesson: Deno.serve() runs one process handling every route, unlike a serverless-functions model where each endpoint is its own deployment; server.ts fakes that separation with an internal route table.

tour.title: Buyer-Facing Channel Handlers
tour.description: These three handlers are where a buyer's message actually enters the system. whatsapp-webhook handles Meta's verification handshake, checks the HMAC signature, and debounces message bursts; telegram-webhook does the equivalent secret-token check for the Telegram bot that emulates WhatsApp in this demo; chat/index.ts exposes a plain HTTP /chat endpoint used by the browser demo. All three do their channel-specific plumbing and then hand off to the exact same shared conversation logic.

tour.title: Payment and Scheduling Webhooks
tour.description: The remaining two edge functions round out the API layer but serve very different triggers. shopify-webhook listens for Shopify's own payment confirmations, verifies the HMAC signature, and records the payment back into the Supabase store. window-scheduler is called by pg_cron/pg_net rather than a buyer: it opens, sweeps, closes, or prunes the weekly order window behind a shared-secret gate, deliberately reusing the same conversation-layer functions the chat flow calls so the money-critical close logic exists in exactly one place.

tour.title: The Conversation State Machine
tour.description: conversation.ts is the single most important file in the project: a roughly 2,400-line dispatcher (handleMessage) that every webhook from Steps 3 and 4 ultimately calls into. It routes incoming buyer and operator text through ordering, discount, promo, and window open/close flows, and exposes the same entry points (sweepWindow, closeOrderWindow, openWindowFor) that window-scheduler uses directly. Everything downstream in this tour is a dependency this file leans on.
tour.languageLesson: A single large dispatch function driven by a stage/step field is a state-machine pattern: instead of scattering conditionals across files, one function owns every legal transition, which is what makes handleMessage testable end to end with fakes.

tour.title: Hexagonal Ports: Store, Messenger, Claude, Shopify
tour.description: This is the architecture README.md promised: conversation.ts never talks to Supabase, WhatsApp, Claude, or Shopify directly, it talks to four interfaces. store.ts abstracts persistence (in-memory fake for tests, Supabase-backed for production). messenger.ts abstracts outbound messaging by recipient ID shape. claude.ts wraps the Claude API with a tool-use schema for order parsing, with a StubParser fallback. shopify.ts builds and creates draft orders against the Shopify Admin API, with a FakeShopify test double. Swapping the live implementation for the fake is what lets the whole order flow run offline.
tour.languageLesson: Hexagonal (ports & adapters) architecture: business logic depends on interfaces it defines, not on concrete external services. Each port pairs a live adapter with a fake adapter behind the same shape, so tests never touch a real network call.

tour.title: Shared Domain Types
tour.description: types.ts is the vocabulary every module from Steps 5 and 6 shares: products, parsed order items, buyers, order windows, group buys, discounts, sessions, audit events, and order records. Notably, money is always represented as integer cents rather than floats, a deliberate choice to avoid rounding bugs in a system that computes group discounts and totals.
tour.languageLesson: Representing currency as integer cents (not float dollars) sidesteps binary floating-point rounding errors, a common source of subtle bugs in commerce code.

tour.title: Group-Buy and Order-Window Math
tour.description: Three modules implement the domain logic that makes this a group-buying app rather than a plain order form. groupbuy.ts validates and generates group-buy IDs and computes aggregate progress against the MOQ (minimum order quantity) threshold. orderwindow.ts computes the current weekly window ID and allocates limited stock across carts, splitting out items that exceed what's left. catalogue.ts is the static fallback product list used when Shopify's live catalogue can't be reached.

tour.title: The Database Schema
tour.description: These four tables from migration 0001 are what store.ts's Supabase implementation (Step 6) actually persists to. buyers is keyed by WhatsApp phone number; group_buys tracks a campaign's status, threshold, and discount rule; sessions holds each buyer's in-progress cart and conversation step between stateless inbound messages; orders mirrors Shopify draft orders with parsed cart items and status. The sessions table in particular is what lets conversation.ts resume a multi-turn chat.
tour.languageLesson: Foreign keys between group_buys, sessions, and orders enforce at the database level the same relationships the domain types in Step 7 model in code, so the schema and the type system stay in sync.

tour.title: Requirements Source of Truth
tour.description: docs/BRS-URS.md is the Business & User Requirement Specification that everything built so far traces back to: 13 functional requirements (FR-1 through FR-13) covering WhatsApp order capture, group buys, pricing, and the admin dashboard. It's worth reading now that you've seen the code, since it explains the *why* behind decisions like the hexagonal ports (Step 6) and the weekly order window (Step 8).

tour.title: The Demo Chat UI
tour.description: index.html is the browser-based stand-in for the real WhatsApp Business chat surface: a WhatsApp-style interface that talks to the chat/index.ts endpoint from Step 3 (or local fakes via `deno task serve`), rendering buyer/bot bubbles alongside a live view of the conversation state machine's stage, cart, and group-buy progress from Step 5. It exists because the live product is WhatsApp Business, which can't easily be demoed live; this page emulates it.

tour.title: Containerization & Local Tooling
tour.description: The Dockerfile packages the whole app (server.ts, static pages, assets, and the Supabase Edge Functions from Steps 2-4) into a single-stage Deno Alpine image that runs as a non-root user, matching server.ts's role as the one Cloud Run front door. deno.json defines the project's task shortcuts (test, serve, simulate, eval, seed-round, start) that wire these pieces together for local development.
tour.languageLesson: Running the container as a non-root user limits blast radius if the process is ever compromised; it's a small addition to a Dockerfile that costs nothing at runtime.

tour.title: Deploying to Cloud Run
tour.description: docs/gcp-deploy.md is the runbook that takes the container image from Step 12 to production: enabling APIs, managing secrets, deploying to Cloud Run, configuring Cloud Scheduler to hit the window-scheduler endpoint from Step 4, repointing webhooks, and rolling back if needed. It's the operational counterpart to the architecture you've just walked through.

tour.title: Testing the NL Parser
tour.description: The eval harness closes the loop on the natural-language parsing from Step 6's claude.ts. tests/evals/eval-set.ts is a ground-truth fixture set pairing buyer messages with expected parsed intent across categories like synonyms, typos, off-catalogue requests, and prompt-injection attempts. tests/evals/run.ts runs the suite against either the StubParser or the live Claude parser, prints a pass/fail report, and exits non-zero if the K1 hallucination gate fails, catching the exact kind of misparse that would silently corrupt an order.
